January 6th, 2025
Position: Lead Autopsy Technician

To Whom It May Concern,
	I am thrilled to present my application for the Lead Autopsy Technician position in Raleigh, North Carolina. Please accept this cover letter and accompanying documents as an indication of my deep interest in this position. 
Since earning my bachelor’s degree in Exercise and Sport Science with an English double major from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, followed by additional STEM courses to complete medical school prerequisites, I have become extremely interested in pathology. My academic career has included six semesters of various anatomy and physiology courses. Most notably, I served as a learning apprentice for a model anatomy lab and participated in a human cadaver laboratory, both of which allowed me to learn more deeply about anatomical structure and function through working with models and human specimens. These are ultimately what piqued my interest in this field. From other STEM courses I learned about various laboratory instruments and techniques, and my English courses greatly strengthened my verbal and written communication. I believe my cumulated knowledge will allow me to serve this position well. 
In my current position as a Cardiology Technician, I have experience with training colleagues, detailed documentation, patient confidentiality, and safety precautions among other skills. It is also worth noting that during my time in this position, I have become close with a colleague whose son unfortunately passed away last year due to gun violence. When she received the autopsy report from your office, she brought it to work and asked me to read through it with her. When her son passed, she had so many unanswered questions, but I witnessed firsthand the clarity and comfort that that autopsy report brought her. While I already knew the importance of such a document, this new perspective resonated with me and made me realize its direct impact and what it means to the families receiving them. I know that this is important work and I want to be a part of it. 
While I know the things I have laid out in this letter do not replace real-world experience in this position, I would be grateful for the opportunity to acquire that real-world experience with your team. I am a quick learner and I truly believe that I can utilize the knowledge and skills that I have acquired to be an asset to your team, while also working in an area that is of great interest to me. I look forward to hearing from you soon!
Best,

Position: Bioprocess Technician IV

To Whom It May Concern,
	I am Jane Doe and I am applying for the Bioprocess Technician IV position in Sanford. Please accept this cover letter, attached resume, and transcript as an indication of my deep interest in this position. Although I do not have experience in this specific position, I hope you will not discount my potential to be a strong team member. 
As detailed in the attached documents, I have a bachelor’s degree in Exercise and Sport Science from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill that includes an array of science courses that built my foundational scientific knowledge and a double major in English that sharpened both my written and verbal communication skills. I also recently returned to UNC and completed additional biology and chemistry courses that encompassed a variety of topics including vaccines and immunology. I am eager to utilize and apply the knowledge I have gained from these rigorous courses and laboratories to help others through the work at your company. 
While I do have direct experience helping others in my current position as a Cardiology Technician at City General Hospital, I am prepared to do something more challenging. It is worth noting that my role there has allowed me to refine my skills in several areas that are listed as crucial to the position for which I am applying, including but certainly not limited to detailed documentation, safety, working as part of a team and on my own, training colleagues, adaptability, troubleshooting, recordkeeping, and attention to detail. I am confident these skills are transferable to your facility and will make me a valuable part of your staff. 
 Having had the opportunity to both learn about vaccines and see their relevance in a clinical setting, I am eager to work more behind-the-scenes. While I know academic courses and my current experience do not replace real-world experience in this specific role, I would be grateful for the opportunity to acquire that real-world experience with your team. I am a quick and motivated learner, and I truly believe that I can be an asset to your team while also gaining experience in an area that is of great interest to me. 
	I hope that you are able to see value in the experience that I do have and how it can be utilized in becoming a strong team member. I look forward to hearing from you soon!

Best,
Jane Doe

April 19th, 2022
Position: Travel Advisor – Raleigh / Durham, NC

To Whom It May Concern,
	I am Jane Doe and I am applying for the Travel Advisor position in the Raleigh / Durham area. Please accept this cover letter and my attached resume as an indication of my deep interest in this position. From looking at my resume, you will see that I have no professional travel advisor experience, although I hope this doesn’t discount my experiences with traveling and travel planning in my personal life. I deeply believe that I can be an asset to your team. 
My love for traveling was first sparked my sophomore year of college when my best friend and I packed our bags and set out for the Grand Canyon on our own at the age of nineteen. We drove from our small town of Seagrove, North Carolina to Flagstaff, Arizona and back over the course of six days. We were exhausted when we got back, but I found myself already excited to plan the next trip. The following fall, I got a group together and we drove to Niagara Falls and back on a long weekend. In October of 2020, my husband and I got married and set out for a two-week honeymoon to the west coast and back. Although we visited many different places, some of the trip highlights include the rolling landscapes of southern Wyoming; the free-spirited Denver and Colorado Springs, Colorado; the wide expanses of the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah which were encapsulated by gorgeous mountains; the bustle of San Francisco, California; the feeling of looking at the Pacific Ocean for the first time, the life-changing seafood on the pier in Santa Cruz, California; the nightlife of Las Vegas, Nevada; the always-breathtaking beauty of the Grand Canyon (yes, again!); and the food in Fort Worth, Texas. After our honeymoon and posting pictures, an acquaintance reached out to me to help her and her fiancé plan their own out-west road trip. The following summer (of 2021), we planned a trip for the Northeast and we drove to Kennebunkport, Maine and back. My road-tripping knowledge has definitely expanded a lot since I first started!
	My experience, however, does not just stop at road-tripping; I have also planned multiple cruises for close family and friends to the Bahamas and Mexico. I was responsible for obtaining everyone’s availability, planning in a way that fit everyone’s schedule, and for handling the financial and personal information needed to plan. I also have some experience with filing travel insurance claims from those family and friends when they needed to cancel. Beyond cruises, I had my first experience with flying earlier this year in March. My husband and I flew to New York City, which was amazing! We already have another trip planned for this summer that will hopefully put us a step closer to our goal of visiting all 50 United States; we are currently at 36 out of 50, but after our summer trip we will hopefully be at 48 out of 50. 
	Despite a lack of professional experience with travel, I do have lots of personal experience that I strongly believe would make me a great asset to your team. I have a broad foundational knowledge of many continental states, as well as different modes of travel. I hope that you are able to see the value in these experiences and how I can use them to best serve your company. I hope to hear from you soon!

Best,
Jane Doe

### Contradictions and Discrepancies

Overall, the documents are highly consistent. There are no major factual contradictions, but there is one minor discrepancy and a clear narrative evolution that could be seen as a discrepancy if not viewed chronologically.

1. **Minor Discrepancy: Number of A&P Courses**
    - **Autopsy Letter Claim:** "My academic career has included **six semesters** of various anatomy and physiology courses."
    - **Transcript Reality (Doc1):** Your undergraduate transcript shows 5 distinct A&P-related courses/sections taken for credit: EXSS 175 (Anatomy), EXSS 276 (Physiology), EXSS 275L (Anatomy Lab), EXSS 376 (Physiology of Performance), and BIOL 252L (A&P Lab).     - **EKG Technician Letter (June 2023):** Your stated goal was to pursue a medical degree with a specialization in **cardiology**. Your motivation was your academic background in exercise physiology and EKG labs.
    - **Autopsy Technician Letter (Jan 2025):** Your stated goal has shifted to becoming a **medical examiner/pathologist**. Your motivation is now a combination of anatomy lab experience and the personal story of helping your colleague.

---

Your narrative integrity is very high. Each cover letter tells a version of a consistent and evolving story, and they align well with the resume and transcripts.

- **Consistency:** The core elements of your background (UNC degrees, Exercise Science/English majors, recent science coursework, Cardiology Tech role, anatomy lab experience) are repeated across documents. - **Compelling Storytelling:** The Autopsy Technician letter stands out for its powerful narrative hook—the story of your colleague. This anecdote provides a strong, emotionally resonant reason for your career change, making your application memorable. It effectively uses your resume's "Other Involvement & Activities" (human cadaver lab, learning apprentice role) as the academic foundation for this new goal.

In conclusion, the documents present a cohesive and credible portrait of a candidate with a dynamic career journey. The minor discrepancy in the course count is negligible, and the evolution of your goals is presented as a natural progression rather than a contradiction.
